source_refs.note: 2. Glycoprotein Hormones: a main subheading of 16.1.1 Chemical Nature of Hormones, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 58-58.

blocks.text: Glycoproteins are "conjugated proteins". They consist of a protein combined with a carbohydrate (sugar) group. They are large, complex, and polar molecules. So, they also cannot pass through the cell membrane. Examples include;

blocks.caption: Glycoprotein hormones
rows: Stimulates the thyroid gland to produce thyroxine.
Stimulates sperm production or egg development.
Triggers ovulation in females and secretion of testosterone in males.
